Tom — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the attachments. High-level response and proposed next steps below.

Short answers up front:
- Burst behavior: Redwood uses adaptive batching + token-level admission with backpressure. For short bursts (~60s) we attempt to absorb via temporary burst capacity and graceful queuing; above configurable thresholds we'll return a 429 with Retry-After. We can show logs from a controlled spike test.
- Failover: we can route to secondary regions automatically per routing policy. Stateful KV caches must be warmed; we recommend a stepped failover test so you can measure cold-cache penalty. We also provide an option to route to a cheaper quantized variant as a degraded mode.
- Telemetry: we will provide token-level latency distributions, 429/5xx counts, and error-budget dashboards (Grafana link in the formal test artifacts).

Proposed immediate plan (owners in parentheses):
1) Baseline throughput: steady-state 500 req/s for 30m — measure p50/p95 latency and CPU/GPU utilization (owner: ben_carter).
2) Burst spike test: ramp 50 -> 2k req/s over 30s, hold 60s, observe throttles and error codes (owner: ben_carter).
3) Multi-region failover: simulate region outage and measure cold-cache latency and failover routing time (owner: marissa_cole).
4) Degraded-mode routing: switch to quantized or lower-tier model when error budget exceeded and measure degradation impact (owner: raFael_mendes).

Can Ben and Marissa take the technical lead on #1-3? I’ll own the fallback/degraded-mode workflows and produce the executive summary for Acme.

I’ll attach a concise test matrix and a load script repo link in the next email. Thoughts on timing — can we run the tests next Tue/Wed (Jul 20–21)?

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Tom / Rafael — attaching the test matrix (acme_test_matrix.xlsx) and load config snippets (load-script-config.yaml, failover-config-snippet.txt). Below is a runnable plan with pass/fail criteria and metrics to collect.

Test matrix (high-level):
- Scenario A — Baseline steady-state
  * Duration: 30m at 500 req/s
  * Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (tokens and request), GPU utilization, queue depth, token cost per 1M
  * Pass criteria: p95 latency < 250ms, 5xx < 0.1%

- Scenario B — Burst spike
  * Ramp: 50 -> 2000 req/s over 30s, hold 60s, then decay
  * Observe: 429 rate, Retry-After behavior, graceful queuing vs immediate rejection
  * Data to capture: per-second QPS, 429 timestamps, rejection TTLs, number of retried requests served

- Scenario C — Region failover
  * Trigger: drain primary region (simulate capacity loss)
  * Observe: time-to-route (ms), cold-KV miss rate, extra-tail latency (p99/p999), cost delta per request after failover
  * Pass criteria: route time < 30s, cold-cache p99 < 5s, no sustained >1% error spike after 5 minutes (unless overloaded)

- Scenario D — Degraded-mode (quantized model fallback)
  * Trigger when error budget exceeds 0.2% per 1h window
  * Observe quality delta (sample prompts), latency gains, cost savings

Telemetry and artifacts we will deliver:
- Per-test Grafana dashboard (latency percentiles, 429/5xx counts, token throughput)
- Raw trace export (jaeger) for 30 minutes around each incident
- Load generator config and runbook (repo link below)

Owners and timeline:
- Ben Carter: test orchestration and load generator (run Tue-Wed, Jul 20–21)
- Marissa Cole: multi-region failover execution and cache-warm benchmarking (Wed afternoon)
- Rafael Mendes: executive summary + cost comparison vs AWS Sagemaker / GCP Vertex by Fri Jul 23

Artifacts attached: acme_test_matrix.xlsx, load-script-config.yaml, failover-config-snippet.txt

Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/acme-poc-load-scripts

Let me know if the pass/fail thresholds look reasonable or if Acme needs stricter windows.

Thanks,
Ben
